newsitem.title: USA: US corporate debt issuers feeding strong demand.
newsitem.headline: US corporate debt issuers feeding strong demand.

text.p: Several debt offerings are on the U.S. corporate bond primary menu, as hungry investors who quickly devoured Wednesday's about $1.0 billion in new issues, crave more, dealers said.
"Demand for corporate paper continues to be very strong and several deals are being worked on currently, to meet demand," said one syndicate source.
First on the new issue plate is Korea Export-Import Bank which is expected to bring its $500 million A1-A-minus rated global 10-year issue, sources said.

In addition, WorldCom Inc is planning to sell $1.5 billion in debt next week. The offering is expected to consist of senior notes with maturities between seven and 10-years and will be underwritten by Salomon Brothers.

WorldCom's offering will be the first since the company's acquisition of MFS Communications Inc last year and will be a partial drawdown from a $3.0 billion shelf registration filed in February, the company said.
Proceeds from the offering will be used primarily for the repayment of bank debt, general corporate purposes and to fund expansion, the firm added.
Still, another $2.3 billion in private placement debt offerings are expected to hit the corporate bond primary market near-term, sources said.
Qwest Communications is expected to bring a $450 million two part 144A debt offering via Salomon Brothers.
The B2/B-plus rated deal consists of $200 million in B2/B-plus rated 10-year senior notes and $250 million (proceeds) of 10-year senior discount notes.
Also, Spanish Broadcasting System is expected to set a $250 million two-part 144A debt offering via sole manager CIBC Wood Gundy.

The deal consist of $75 million in senior notes due 2004, price talk is seen at 10.50 percent area. The second tranche for $175 million is for senior exchange pik preferred securities. Price talk is seen between 13.25 - 13.50 percent.

Central Tractor Farm & Country Inc is also expected to issue $100 million in B1/B-plus rated senior notes due 2007 via Nationsbanc Capital markets, sources said. Price talk on the issue is 10.50 to 10.75 percent.
Intercel Inc said it also planned to issue $300 million in senior notes due 2007 via Morgan Stanley & Co.
